correctness.rationale: The numerical rational counterexample itself is correct: eigenvalues of P are 2,1, Q are 39/20,1/20, and <Pf,Qf> at (1,-3/2) is -1/40. However the advertised universal exact repair iff Q S_Lambda P∈GL+(H) is FALSE in the expressly real Hilbert-space setting. Set S_Lambda=I, P=diag(2,1), Q=[[1,1/10],[1/10,1]]; QP=[[2,1/10],[1/5,1]] is nonsymmetric, hence not GL+, while every real quadratic value <Pf,Qf>=f^T((QP+PQ)/2)f is bounded above and below by positive multiples of ||f||², because symmetric part [[2,3/20],[3/20,1]] has positive trace and determinant 791/400. Correct real iff condition is positivity of the symmetric part, not self-adjointness of QSP. In complex Hilbert spaces the requirement of real quadratic energy is different. The package does not distinguish these settings. A partial correct counterexample cannot validate the complete final claim; no full scientific correction with all affected files was staged.
residual_risks: Real vs complex Hilbert quadratic positivity is essential; the false iff covers the explicitly real setting.
